title: Chiyya bar Rav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman considers it very likely that he was born after Rabbi Chiyya’s death, and Rav named him after his uncle. His father Rav studied with him, as in Berakhot 53b and Nazir 66b, where he said to him, “My son, seize [the cup] and bless”; in Pesachim 70a, “Rav taught Chiyya his son”; there, 113a, Rav said to him, “Do not drink drugs,” etc.; and in Moed Katan 20a he said to him, “In her presence observe mourning.” Likewise he raised objections to Rav Assi, as in Ketubot 48b, Kiddushin 46a and Keritot 17b. He likewise sat before Shmuel, as in Arakhin 16b, and Shmuel said to him, “Son of a lion” or “son of the learned, come and I will tell you a fine thing that Rav your father used to say,” as in Berakhot 12a, Chagigah 14a and Avodah Zarah 31b.

In Hyman’s account, all the great students of Rav were his teachers, as in Eruvin 47a, “Rav Chiyya bar Ashi taught Chiyya bar Rav before Rav”; in Eruvin 98b and the Jerusalem Talmud there, 1:1, with the additional locator ה., “Rav Chinena bar Shelamya taught him before Rav”; in Shabbat 66a and Yoma 15b, “Rav Chanan bar Rava taught him before Rav”; in Eruvin 2b and 14a, “Rav Yehudah taught him before Rav”; and in Avodah Zarah 4:8, “Shimon bar Chiyya taught him.” With Rav Huna he was like a colleague, for both sat before Shmuel, as in Arakhin 16b; their disputes are in Shabbat 69b, Bava Batra 4b and Avodah Zarah 49b; in Chullin 14a, “Rav Huna said: Chiyya bar Rav expounded in Rav’s name.” Hyman explains that only because Rav Huna headed the academy in Sura do we find in Bekhorot 22a that he called Rav Huna “my teacher.” It likewise appears from Bava Batra 39b that Chiyya bar Rav sat with Rav Huna, for they said there: “Giddel bar Minyomi … found Rav Huna, Chiyya bar Rav and Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi”; and so it is in the Jerusalem Talmud there, 3:3: “Giddul bar Minyamin had a case, and his judges were Chilkiyah bar Tuvi, Rav Huna and Chiyya bar Rav.” Hyman describes his halakhot as few, saying that he is mentioned only in Berakhot 14b, and Rav Huna bar Chinena spoke in his name, as in Berakhot 30a; Rabbah bar Avuha asked him, as in Avodah Zarah 51a; and we likewise find Abaye in his name, as in Shevuot 17b. In Sukkah we find that he disagrees with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, but Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi. Of his personal events we find in Yevamot 63a: when he saw that his mother was distressing his father, always doing the opposite of his father’s wish — when Rav wanted lentils, she made peas — what did he do? He told his mother that his father wanted peas, and she made lentils as his father wished. His father, who did not know that it was his son’s cleverness, said to him that his mother’s heart had turned for the good. Then his son told him that it was by his cleverness. Rav said to him: “This is what people say: The one who comes from you teaches you sense. But you, do not do so,” so as not to train oneself to speak falsehood.

In Gittin 18a: his ketubah was written by day and signed at night, and Rav was there. At the supplied locator בב״ק פ״טז־ג [it is related] that Rav said to him, “Build me a house in the Land of Israel.” He merited a son great in Torah named Shimi, who was dear to Rav his grandfather, as in Kiddushin 12a.
